Low-speed centrifugation separates cellular components based on size and density differences.  
Nuclei are large and dense, while secretory vesicles are small and less dense, so they would separate at low speeds.  
DNA and mRNA are too similar in size and would not separate this way.  
Golgi apparatus and endoplasmic reticulum have overlapping sizes/densities and require higher-resolution methods.  
Lysosomes and endosomes are similar in size and density, so they would not separate well at low speeds.  

Final answer: (B)
